subject.title: Design: Telegram isolated ingress holds per-chat lane for the entire agent turn — long turns block the group, then die at 25 min

question: Should Telegram isolated ingress release the per-chat/topic spool lane after durable handoff to session admission instead of after the full agent turn completes?
rationale: The source-level failure is clear, but the permanent fix changes Telegram transport ordering, duplicate/replay safety, timeout semantics, and downstream session admission ownership, so maintainers need to choose the contract before implementation.

options.title: Detach after durable handoff
options.body: Move Telegram spool lane lifetime to ingestion/classification plus durable session handoff, then let session admission own active-run ordering and steering.

options.title: Keep lane ownership
options.body: Preserve one-handler-per-lane through the full turn and address only watchdog, visibility, or dead-letter symptoms.

options.title: Split narrower follow-ups
options.body: Track timeout visibility, collect starvation, and claude-cli steering injection separately while leaving this issue as the lane-ownership design decision.

recommendation.title: Detach after durable handoff
recommendation.body: Move Telegram spool lane lifetime to ingestion/classification plus durable session handoff, then let session admission own active-run ordering and steering.

likelyOwner.reason: They are assigned to this issue and have the strongest recent history on the current Telegram lane code and adjacent run-lifecycle work.
